Standard Library: Regularity

Abbreviation 44
elemminimal

$a$ is an \in-minimal element of $A$ iff $a\class{latex-symbol-tip latex-symbol-id-in}{\in} A$ and $a\notmeets A$.

LaTeX source 
\begin{abbreviation}
\label{elemminimal}
    $a$ is an \in-minimal element of $A$ iff
    $a\in A$ and $a\notmeets A$.
\end{abbreviation}
Lemma 1232
regularity_aux

Let $A$ be a set.
For all $a\class{latex-symbol-tip latex-symbol-id-in}{\in} A$ there exists $b\class{latex-symbol-tip latex-symbol-id-in}{\in} A$ such that $b\notmeets A$.

LaTeX source 
\begin{lemma}
\label{regularity_aux}
    Let $A$ be a set.
    For all $a\in A$ there exists $b\in A$ such that
    $b\notmeets A$.
\end{lemma}
Proof
Case. $a\notmeets A$.

Take $b$ such that $b = a$.
Straightforward.

Case. $a\meets A$.

Take $a'$ such that $a'\class{latex-symbol-tip latex-symbol-id-in}{\in} a, A$.
There exists $b\class{latex-symbol-tip latex-symbol-id-in}{\in} A$ such that $b\notmeets A$.

LaTeX source 
\begin{byCase}
        \caseOf{$a\notmeets A$.}
            Take $b$ such that $b = a$.
            Straightforward.
        \caseOf{$a\meets A$.}
            Take $a'$ such that $a'\in a, A$.
            There exists $b\in A$ such that $b\notmeets A$.
    
\end{byCase}
LaTeX source 
\begin{proof}
[Proof by \in-induction on $a$]
    \begin{byCase}
        \caseOf{$a\notmeets A$.}
            Take $b$ such that $b = a$.
            Straightforward.
        \caseOf{$a\meets A$.}
            Take $a'$ such that $a'\in a, A$.
            There exists $b\in A$ such that $b\notmeets A$.
    \end{byCase}
\end{proof}
Proposition 409 [Regularity]
regularity

Let $A$ be an inhabited set.
Then there exists a \in-minimal element of $A$.

LaTeX source 
\begin{proposition}
[Regularity]
\label{regularity}
    Let $A$ be an inhabited set.
    Then there exists a \in-minimal element of $A$.
\end{proposition}
Proof

Follows by Lemma 1232.

LaTeX source 
\begin{proof}
    Follows by \cref{regularity_aux}.
\end{proof}
Theorem 144 [Foundation]
foundation

Let $A$ be a set.
Then $A = \class{latex-symbol-tip latex-symbol-id-emptyset}{\emptyset}$ or there exists $a\class{latex-symbol-tip latex-symbol-id-in}{\in} A$ such that for all $x\class{latex-symbol-tip latex-symbol-id-in}{\in} a$ we have $x\class{latex-symbol-tip latex-symbol-id-notin}{\notin} A$.

LaTeX source 
\begin{theorem}
[Foundation]\label{foundation}
    Let $A$ be a set.
    Then $A = \emptyset$ or there exists $a\in A$
    such that for all $x\in a$ we have $x\notin A$.
\end{theorem}
Proof
Case. $A = \class{latex-symbol-tip latex-symbol-id-emptyset}{\emptyset}$.

Follows by assumption.

Case. $A \class{latex-symbol-tip latex-symbol-id-neq}{\neq}\class{latex-symbol-tip latex-symbol-id-emptyset}{\emptyset}$.

Take $a$ such that $a$ is a \in-minimal element of $A$ by Proposition 10, Proposition 409 [Regularity].
Then for all $x\class{latex-symbol-tip latex-symbol-id-in}{\in} a$ we have $x\class{latex-symbol-tip latex-symbol-id-notin}{\notin} A$.
Follows by assumption.

LaTeX source 
\begin{byCase}
        \caseOf{$A = \emptyset$.}
            Follows by assumption.
        \caseOf{$A \neq\emptyset$.}
            Take $a$ such that $a$ is a \in-minimal element of $A$ by \cref{nonempty_inhabited,regularity}.
            Then for all $x\in a$ we have $x\notin A$.
            Follows by assumption.
    
\end{byCase}
LaTeX source 
\begin{proof}
    \begin{byCase}
        \caseOf{$A = \emptyset$.}
            Follows by assumption.
        \caseOf{$A \neq\emptyset$.}
            Take $a$ such that $a$ is a \in-minimal element of $A$ by \cref{nonempty_inhabited,regularity}.
            Then for all $x\in a$ we have $x\notin A$.
            Follows by assumption.
    \end{byCase}
\end{proof}

Proposition 419
suc_injective

Suppose $\suc{x} = \suc{y}$.
Then $x = y$.

LaTeX source 
\begin{proposition}
\label{suc_injective}
    Suppose $\suc{x} = \suc{y}$. Then $x = y$.
\end{proposition}
Proof

Suppose not.
$\suc{x}\class{latex-symbol-tip latex-symbol-id-subseteq}{\subseteq} \suc{y}$.
Hence $x\class{latex-symbol-tip latex-symbol-id-in}{\in}\suc{y}$.
Then $x\class{latex-symbol-tip latex-symbol-id-in}{\in} y$.
$\suc{y}\class{latex-symbol-tip latex-symbol-id-subseteq}{\subseteq} \suc{x}$.
Hence $y\class{latex-symbol-tip latex-symbol-id-in}{\in}\suc{x}$.
Then $y\class{latex-symbol-tip latex-symbol-id-in}{\in} x$.
Contradiction.

LaTeX source 
\begin{proof}
    Suppose not.
    $\suc{x}\subseteq \suc{y}$. Hence $x\in\suc{y}$.
    Then $x\in y$.
    $\suc{y}\subseteq \suc{x}$. Hence $y\in\suc{x}$.
    Then $y\in x$.
    Contradiction.
\end{proof}
